Abstract
A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization (LC-APCI-MS). This study employs high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to a quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometer (HPLC-QTOF MS) to analyze the secondary metabolites produced by *C. nivalis*. Specifically, this approach focuses on the detection and characterization of astaxanthin diglucoside diesters, which have not been previously identified in this algal species. The use of atmospheric pressure chemical ionization (APCI) enables the generation of molecular ions through proton transfer, facilitating the accurate determination of molecular weights and fragmentation patterns that distinguish between isomeric compounds. The results provide novel insights into the biosynthetic pathways and potential ecological roles of these unique metabolites in polar environments. These findings contribute to our understanding of the biochemical adaptations of polar microalgae to extreme conditions and may have implications for biotechnological applications in natural product discovery and synthetic biology.

generations.raw_text: Skin biopsy homogenates obtained from three cases of lepromatous leprosy with no prior history of antileprosy treatment were tested in the mouse footpad for the sensitivity of Mycobacterium leprae to multiple drugs. This study aimed to investigate the primary drug resistance patterns of M. leprae in untreated lepromatous leprosy patients, as well as to assess the susceptibility profiles when individual drugs were tested in combination. The results revealed a spectrum of resistance to first-line drugs ( rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone), indicating the presence of primary resistance. Furthermore, synergistic and antagonistic effects were observed among different combinations of these drugs, highlighting the complexity of therapeutic strategies against M. leprae. These findings underscore the importance of early and accurate drug sensitivity testing to guide effective treatment protocols for leprosy. The mouse footpad model served as an efficient in vivo assay system, providing insights into the pathogenesis and drug resistance mechanisms of leprosy at its primary site of infection. This study contributes to the understanding of drug-resistant strains and the development of improved treatment regimens for this debilitating disease.

generations.raw_text: Currently, traditional family values that have been passed down through generations appear to be at risk, posing significant implications for the stability and health of individuals, families, and communities. This article explores selected issues related to intergenerational transmission of family values, focusing on the role of family traditions in preserving cultural heritage and fostering family cohesion across different generations. Through an integrative review of existing literature and qualitative case studies, we examine how modernization, migration, and changing social dynamics are affecting the continuity and adaptation of family traditions. The study highlights the importance of understanding and preserving family traditions as a means to maintain social bonds and enhance psychological well-being. Our findings suggest that efforts to revitalize and reinterpret family traditions can play a crucial role in bridging generational gaps and enhancing intergenerational relationships. This research underscores the need for further interdisciplinary exploration into the mechanisms and strategies for sustaining family traditions in the face of contemporary challenges.

generations.raw_text: As a member of the testis-specific serine/threonine protein kinase (TSSK) family, Tssk4 is exclusively expressed in the testis and plays an essential role in male fertility. We previously reported that Tssk4 is involved in spermatogenesis through the regulation of sperm tail development, but the specific mechanisms underlying its function remain largely unknown. In this study, we focused on elucidating the molecular mechanism by which Tssk4 modulates male fertility. We found that Tssk4 directly phosphorylates Odf2 (Outer Dense Fiber Protein 2) at Ser-76. Our results demonstrate that this phosphorylation event significantly enhances the interaction between Odf2 and its binding partner, the dynein intermediate chain (Dyic). The enhanced interaction subsequently leads to the proper localization and organization of outer dense fibers, which are crucial for the assembly and motility of the sperm flagellum. Moreover, we observed that Tssk4-deficient mice exhibit impaired sperm motility, further supporting the importance of Odf2 phosphorylation by Tssk4 in male fertility. These findings not only provide new insights into the molecular basis of Tssk4's role in spermatogenesis but also suggest that Tssk4-Odf2 signaling may represent a promising therapeutic target for male infertility.

generations.raw_text: The case of a young female patient with acute symmetrical ascending polyneuropathy as a manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is reported. There was involvement of several cranial nerves, including the facial, glossopharyngeal, vagus, and accessory nerves, indicating a multifocal neuropathic process. The cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed elevated protein levels (102 mg/dL; normal range 15-45 mg/dL) with a mild pleocytosis (10 cells/µL; normal range <10 cells/µL). Anti-GQ1b antibodies were negative, ruling out Guillain-Barré syndrome of the Miller Fisher variant. The patient also presented with malar rash, oral ulcers, and photosensitivity, consistent with an SLE diagnosis. Comprehensive immunosuppressive therapy with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and corticosteroids led to partial recovery of neurologic function within 6 weeks, though residual weakness persisted. This case highlights the potential overlap between Guillain-Barré syndrome and SLE, emphasizing the importance of a detailed clinical evaluation and appropriate diagnostic workup in patients presenting with atypical neuropathy.

By analyzing these data, we have investigated the structure and dynamics of the 2-phonon GDR in 208Pb. Our findings reveal the role of two-phonon configurations in the excitation spectrum and offer new information on the coupling strength between the phonon modes and the collective oscillations of the nuclear matter. This work provides a deeper understanding of the low-energy nuclear excitations and their relation to collective motion in heavy nuclei.
